# core/sha256.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/sha256.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4) and HMAC-SHA-256 (RFC 2104).

What is proved: every access is in bounds, nothing leaks, and a digest is
32 bytes. Not proved: that the digest is SHA-256's (the tests check the
FIPS 180-4 and RFC 4231 vectors, including the block-boundary lengths 55,
56, 63, 64 and 65, and a million `a`s), or that the code takes the same
time for every input (it does not branch on its data, but nothing checks
that).

`import "core/sha256.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/endian.bastio](core-endian.md), [core/text.bastio](core-text.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`sha256`](#sha256) | The SHA-256 digest of `m`. |
| [`hmac_sha256`](#hmac_sha256) | HMAC-SHA-256 of `msg` under `key` (any length). |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Functions

### `sha256`

```bastio
fn sha256(m: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  ensures blen(result) == 32
```

The SHA-256 digest of `m`: 32 bytes.

Example:

```bastio
let m = bfrom("abc");
let d = sha256(m);
let first = bget(d, 0);          // ba 78 16 bf ... 15 ad
let last = bget(d, 31);
let n = blen(d);
bfree(d);
bfree(m);
if n != 32 || first != 186 || last != 173 { return 1; }
```

### `hmac_sha256`

```bastio
fn hmac_sha256(key: &Bytes, msg: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  ensures blen(result) == 32
```

HMAC-SHA-256 of `msg` under `key` (any length): 32 bytes.

Example:

```bastio
let key = bfrom("key");
let msg = bfrom("The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog");
let mac = hmac_sha256(key, msg);
let first = bget(mac, 0);        // f7 bc 83 f4 ... d8
let last = bget(mac, 31);
bfree(mac);
bfree(key);
bfree(msg);
if first != 247 || last != 216 { return 1; }
```

## Internals

### `sha256_k`

```bastio
fn sha256_k() -> Vec[u32]
  ensures vlen(result) == 64
```

Internal: the round constants.

### `sha256_rotr`

```bastio
fn sha256_rotr(x: u32, n: u64) -> u32
  requires n >= 1 && n <= 31
```

Internal: `x` rotated right by `n` bits, 1 to 31.

### `sha256_block`

```bastio
fn sha256_block(h: &mut Vec[u32], k: &Vec[u32], w: &mut Vec[u32], m: &Bytes, at: u64)
  requires vlen(h) == 8 && vlen(k) == 64 && vlen(w) == 64 && at + 64 <= blen(m)
  ensures vlen(h) == 8 && vlen(w) == 64
```

Internal: the eight state words after the 64-byte block at `at` of `m`.
